meta.title: Directive (EU) 2016/1919 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 October 2016 on legal aid for suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and for requested persons in European arrest warrant proceedings

items.heading: Article 1

nationalActs.title: Costituzione italiana

provisions.textEn: The indigent are assured, by appropriate measures, the means for legal action and defence in all levels of jurisdiction.

nationalActs.eli: Art. 24, co. 3, Cost. The   indigent   are   assured,   by   appropriate   measures,   the  means  for  legal  action  and  defence  in  all  levels  of  jurisdiction.

provisions.comment:
The Italian legal sistem guarantees to the indigents the right to defend themselves in court in any jurisdiction, not only in criminal proceedings. From this perspective, it recognises a broader right than that of the directive, which could already be said to have been indirectly transposed, now moreover fully transposed by Legislative Decree No. 24 of 2019.

The domestic rules on legal aid, it should be noted, are also distinguished by a certain breadth of protection.

Although the Directive is dedicated to suspects or defendants in a criminal trial, it is worth pointing out that for certain crimes, such as domestic violence, gender-based violence and sexual offences, legal aid is available regardless of any income condition. In these cases, under Article 74(4)(ter) of Presidential Decree 115/2002,  legal aid is available regardless of incom.

Finally, conditions aimed at facilitating access to legal aid are found in favour of minors suspects and defendants (see Articles 116 and 118 Presidential Decree 115/2002).

items.comment: The Italian legal order already recognizes access to legal aid, the change introduced by legislative decree no. 24/2019 completed the audience of recipients. Moreover, from some points of view, the Italian legislation, as recently integrated, has the merit of having expanded the number of wider recipients. In Italy, in fact, self-defense is not permitted in the criminal trial, where defense is always technical.

items.text: 1. This Directive applies to suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings who have a right of access to a lawyer pursuant to Directive 2013/48/EU and who are:
(a)deprived of liberty;
(b)required to be assisted by a lawyer in accordance with Union or national law; or
(c)required or permitted to attend an investigative or evidence-gathering act, including as a minimum the following:
(i)identity parades;
(ii)confrontations;
(iii)reconstructions of the scene of a crime.
2. This Directive also applies, upon arrest in the executing Member State, to requested persons who have a right of access to a lawyer pursuant to Directive 2013/48/EU.

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons who lack sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a lawyer have the right to legal aid when the interests of justice so require.
2. Member States may apply a means test, a merits test, or both to determine whether legal aid is to be granted in accordance with paragraph 1.

provisions.textEn: Admission to legal aid is excluded: a) for the sentenced person with final judgment of crimes committed in violation of the rules for the repression of tax and income tax evasion added (...);

items.comment:
The legal aid discipline (DPR 115/2002) already identifies the conditions for admission to the benefit. The legislative decree 24/2019 has modified the art. 91, DPR 115/2002, which deals with cases of exclusion from legal aid.

Art. 91 DPR 115/2002 states that the admission to legal aid is excluded (a) for persons convicted by a final judgment of offences committed in breach of the rules for preventing the evasion of income tax and value added tax.

items.text: 3. Where a Member State applies a means test, it shall take into account all relevant and objective factors, such as the income, capital and family situation of the person concerned, as well as the costs of the assistance of a lawyer and the standard of living in that Member State, in order to determine whether, in accordance with the applicable criteria in that Member State, a suspect or an accused person lacks sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a lawyer.

nationalActs.title: Decreto Presidente della Repubblica 30 maggio 2002, n. 115

provisions.comment: The assessment of the conditions is carried out in concrete terms, as recently affirmed by the court of cassation (no. 37007/2019), where it is stated that to be admitted to legal aid, the income conditions set out in art. 76, Presidential Decree 115/2002, must be respected. For these purposes, reference is made to the last tax return, but the applicant, even when the value of the tax return is higher than the permitted one, is admitted to prove that he suffered a significant and supervening decrease such as to bring below the threshold of income required by the standard.

items.text: 4. Where a Member State applies a merits test, it shall take into account the seriousness of the criminal offence, the complexity of the case and the severity of the sanction at stake, in order to determine whether the interests of justice require legal aid to be granted. In any event, the merits test shall be deemed to have been met in the following situations:
(a)where a suspect or an accused person is brought before a competent court or judge in order to decide on detention at any stage of the proceedings within the scope of this Directive; and
(b)during detention.

5. Member States shall ensure that legal aid is granted without undue delay, and at the latest before questioning by the police, by another law enforcement authority or by a judicial authority, or before the investigative or evidence-gathering acts referred to in point (c) of Article 2(1) are carried out.
6. Legal aid shall be granted only for the purposes of the criminal proceedings in which the person concerned is suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Legal aid in European arrest warrant proceedings

provisions.textEn: The legal aid discipline also applies to passive delivery procedures, as per law 22 April 2005, no. 69, from the moment of arrest carried out in accordance with the European arrest warrant until delivery or until the moment in which the decision on the non-surrender becomes definitive, as well as in the active delivery procedures, referred to in the aforementioned law n. 69 of 2005, in favor of the wanted person subject to a European arrest warrant execution procedure for the purpose of the prosecution and who has exercised the right to appoint a defender on the national territory to assist the defender in the Executing Member State.

items.text: 1. The executing Member State shall ensure that requested persons have a right to legal aid upon arrest pursuant to a European arrest warrant until they are surrendered, or until the decision not to surrender them becomes final.

2. The issuing Member State shall ensure that requested persons who are the subject of European arrest warrant proceedings for the purpose of conducting a criminal prosecution and who exercise their right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State to assist the lawyer in the executing Member State in accordance with Article 10(4) and (5) of Directive 2013/48/EU have the right to legal aid in the issuing Member State for the purpose of such proceedings in the executing Member State, in so far as legal aid is necessary to ensure effective access to justice.
3. The right to legal aid referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 may be subject to a means test in accordance with Article 4(3), which shall apply mutatis mutandis.

items.subHeading: Decisions regarding the granting of legal aid

provisions.textEn:
Decision on the application for admission to legal aid

Was presented or received, the magistrate before whom the trial hangs (...) having verified the admissibility of the application, admits the interested party to legal aid if, like the substitute declaration provided for by article 79, paragraph 1, letter c), the income conditions are met which the admission to the benefit it is subordinate.

items.text: 1. Decisions on whether or not to grant legal aid and on the assignment of lawyers shall be made, without undue delay, by a competent authority. Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that the competent authority takes its decisions diligently, respecting the rights of the defence.
2. Member States shall take necessary measures to ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons are informed in writing if their request for legal aid is refused in full or in part.

items.heading: Article 7
items.subHeading: Quality of legal aid services and training
items.comment:
PARTIAL IMPLEMENTATION

The Italian legal system concerning the quality of legal aid services is not derived from the transposition of the Directive, and was preexisting.

In the current system, while a specific procedure is established, that should discard unsuitable lawyer from providing legal aid services, nothing at all is recognized to ensure adequate training to the latter (unless they are also appointed ex officio), or to the judges that need to take a decision on the matter.

items.text: 1. Member States shall take necessary measures, including with regard to funding, to ensure that:

nationalActs.title: Decreto Presidente della Repubblica 30 maggio 2002, n. 115

provisions.textEn: A person granted legal aid may appoint a lawyer from the list of legal aid lawyers maintained by the Bar Councils in the district of the Court of Appeal where the court having jurisdiction as to the substance of the matter or the court before which the case is pending, is sitting.

1. The list of lawyers that may be appointed for legal aid shall be made up of lawyers who apply for it and who meet the requirements laid down in paragraph 2.

2. Inclusion on the list shall be decided by the Bar Council, which shall assess whether the following requirements and conditions are met:

(a) aptitude and specific professional experience, distinguishing between civil, criminal, administrative, accounting, tax and voluntary jurisdiction proceedings;

b) absence of disciplinary sanctions of more than a warning imposed in the five years preceding the application;

(c) registration in the Bar for at least two years.

3. A lawyer who has been subjected to a disciplinary sanction of more than a warning shall be automatically removed from the list.

4. The list is renewed by 31 January of each year, is public, and is kept in all the judicial offices located in the territory of each province.

items.text: (a)there is an effective legal aid system that is of an adequate quality; and
(b)legal aid services are of a quality adequate to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, with due respect for the independence of the legal profession.
2. Member States shall ensure that adequate training is provided to staff involved in the decision-making on legal aid in criminal proceedings and in European arrest warrant proceedings.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: No specific training is foreseen for the judges that have to decide over the admission or refusal of legal aid.

items.text: 3. With due respect for the independence of the legal profession and for the role of those responsible for the training of lawyers, Member States shall take appropriate measures to promote the provision of adequate training to lawyers providing legal aid services.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
No specific provision has been introduced to ensure that lawyers providing legal aid services enjoy adequate training. In this sense, it is considered enough the self-declaration of the lawyer that s/he possess sufficient expertise, at least two-years professional working-time and had not been targeted before by disciplinary sanctions (art. 91, DPR 115/2002).


Different is instead the case in which the lawyer, providing legal aid services, is also appointed ex officio by the court. In this situation, in fact, specific training is requested (cfr. Law 247/2012).

items.text: 4. Member States shall take the necessary measures to ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons have the right, upon their request, to have the lawyer providing legal aid services assigned to them replaced, where the specific circumstances so justify.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons have an effective remedy under national law in the event of a breach of their rights under this Directive.
items.heading: Article 8

nationalActs.title: Decreto Presidente della Repubblica 30 maggio 2002, n. 115

provisions.textEn:
1. The interested party may appeal against the decision by which the competent magistrate rejects the application for admission, within twenty days of being informed in accordance with Article 97, before the President of the Court or the President of the Court of Appeal to which the magistrate who issued the rejection decree belongs.

2. The appeal shall be served on the financial office which is a party to the relevant proceedings.

3. The procedure shall be the special procedure established to debate for lawyers' fees and the court shall proceed as a single judge.

4. The order deciding on the appeal shall be notified within ten days, by the office of the prosecuting magistrate, to the person concerned and to the financial office, which, within the following twenty days, may lodge an appeal for cassation on the grounds of violation of the law. The appeal shall not suspend the execution of the measure.

The judge shall declare the application inadmissible or grant or refuse admission to legal aid by means of a reasoned decree, which shall be deposited ( i.e. made accessible to the parties). Copies thereof may be extracted by the person concerned or by his/her lawyer; the person concerned shall be notified thereof.

provisions.comment: Also in case the legal aid is first granted, and then revoked.
provisions.textEn: Against the decree deciding on the request for revocation pursuant to letter d), paragraph 1, of article 112, the interested party may lodge an appeal in Corte di Cassazione [the Italian Supreme Court], without suspensive effect, within twenty days from the notification received pursuant to article 97.

items.comment:
PARTIAL IMPLEMENTATION

The pre-existing regulation on legal aid seems to already provide some regulation, which however does not cover satisfactorily the standards required by EU legislation.

Arts 99 and 113, c. 1, DPR 115/2002, indeed, establish that interested parties may appeal against the decision rejecting the application for admission to the legal aid service. The appeal shall be filed within twenty days from the notification of the rejection, and before the President of the Court or the President of the Court of Appeal to which the judge who issued the rejection decision belongs. The decision on the appeal can be further challenged before the Supreme Court.

Although formally compliant with the Directive, several critical aspects have been highlighted in this regard by legal scholars (cfr. among others, Grisonich, L’attuazione della direttiva, cit, p. 229; Peloso, L’approvazione della direttiva 2016/1919 sul patrocinio a spese dello Stato: la battuta finale nel cammino verso la mappatura dei diritti procedurali fondamentali, in www.lagislazionepenale.eu, 4 maggio 2017, p. 25; Dipaola, Difesa d’ufficio e patrocinio dei non abbienti nel processo penale, 3aed., Milano, 2016, p. 92).

items.text: Member States shall ensure that the particular needs of vulnerable suspects, accused persons and requested persons are taken into account in the implementation of this Directive.
items.heading: Article 9

nationalActs.title: Decreto Presidente della Repubblica 30 maggio 2002, n. 115

provisions.comment: Recognition of the right to legal aid also for foreign unaccompanied minors (situation related to migration phenomena)
provisions.textEn: The unaccompanied foreign minor involved in any capacity in a judicial proceeding shall have the right to [...] to avail himself of free legal aid at any stage and level of the proceedings, in accordance with the legislation in force [...]

1. The fees and expenses payable to the court-appointed child advocate shall be paid by the judge in the amount and according to the procedures envisaged in Article 82 and an objection may be lodged pursuant to Article 84.

2. At the same time as the communication of the payment order, the office shall request the family members of the minor to submit, within one month, the documentation provided for in Article 79 (1) (c); on expiry of the time limit, the office shall request the financial office to fulfil the obligations provided for in Article 98 (2), transmitting any documentation received.

3. The State shall have the right to recover the sums advanced to the minor and his/her family members, if the judge, by decree, establishes that the income limits envisaged for eligibility for legal aid in criminal proceedings have been exceeded, on the basis of the documentation requested from the beneficiaries or on the basis of the financial assessments.

In applying the measures provided for in the DPR 22 September 1988, No 448 [i.e. juvenile criminal procedure law], the expenses for placing the minor in a different place from the family home and for any other activity of observation, treatment and support, are paid by the State.

items.comment:
The Italian legal order provides for an income limit to have access to legal aid when it comes to adult defendant. In the case of minors, the tax documentation of family members must be submitted.

However, artt. 116 and 118 of Presidential Decree no. 115/2002 grant additional margin to the accused minors in case of court-appointed lawyer. In these cases, the State advances the costs and fees to the lawyer of the minor and then has the right to recover the amount paid if the judge establishes that the income limits for admission to legal aid are exceeded. In these situations, it is therefore the State itself that must take steps to verify the existence of the conditions for the repayment of the sums, since the minor or his/her family members do not have to submit any application for admission to legal aid (on the contrary, in the case of the adult, it is the defendant who must take steps to avoid the repayment of the sums by the State).
